content:
Hello,
I need to do differential fuzzing on some Rust code with a Lean oracle. My issue is the startup cost of Lean which slows everything down, therefore the idea is to use the compiled C code to solve this issue, is there any way of doing this (knowing that my Lean code does not only use primitive types) ?
In case this is the wrong channel to ask I am glad to move the message to another one.
Thank you for your help!!
What do you mean by "using it" here? You can just compile it to a binary and run that of course.
Yes sure, but what takes most time is initialize the lean runtime (even if it is a binary). So I was wondering if there is any solution of bypassing this runtime initialization?

You have to do it once per process whenever that process invokes Lean code either directly as a binary or FFI. Though one could imagine a system where you have a parent process that's already initialized and forks of a new lean child I guess?
Yes indeed, that is an option. Thank you for your answer!
